rebuttal_or_critique: I remain firmly of the view that the 'withdrawal of accommodation' stance is no longer appropriate. With core inflation at 3.25%, the real policy rate is already significantly restrictive. The persistence of food inflation at 8.52% is a supply-side issue that cannot be effectively managed through further monetary tightening without inflicting unnecessary damage on the 6.30% GVA growth momentum. A neutral stance is the only logical reflection of a policy rate that has already achieved its restrictive objective. I must dissent from the majority's insistence on maintaining a stance that signals further tightening when the data suggests we have reached a sufficient level of restraint.
